hero_short: AI now drafts the résumés and the cover letters, so sounding capable has never been cheaper. A senior professional has to show the work instead, and I chose to lead that shift rather than wait for it. This site is my most advanced front-end build to date and the most important piece of my personal brand, designed and built by me with AI in five months. Scroll on for why it had to exist, how it grew from a single page, how it was built, and the figures that prove it.
act0_verdict: AI is rewriting work faster than careers can adapt.
act0_lede: Three shifts that make a proven personal brand urgent in 2026.
act0_s1_t: A fifth of jobs in motion
act0_s1_x: By 2030, 22% of today's jobs will be disrupted, with 170 million created and 92 million displaced, and 39% of the skills workers rely on are expected to change.
act0_s2_x: Young workers in the most AI-exposed jobs lost 13% of their employment since 2022, though the cause may not be AI alone. Across Latin America, 26–38% of jobs are exposed to generative AI; in Lima, the under-25 share of work has fallen by about a third since 2019.
act0_s3_x: 66% of leaders would not hire someone without AI skills, and 71% would choose a less experienced candidate who has them. Differentiation for 2027 has to be shown, not claimed, in 2026.
act0_foot: Sources: World Economic Forum, Future of Jobs Report 2025; Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Atkinson and Yamco, 6 January 2026; ILO and World Bank, Working Paper 121, 2024; Microsoft and LinkedIn, Work Trend Index 2024; INEI, Encuesta Permanente de Empleo Nacional, May–July 2026.
act1_verdict: Credentials open the door. They don't prove what I can build.
act1_lede: Three reasons a strong résumé is no longer enough.
act1_s1_x: Job posts spell out what a candidate must have, never how they are expected to think or sound. Meeting every requirement gets an application read; being understood gets it believed.
act1_s2_x: Despite their value, not a single one of my flagship academic credentials (an MBA, a MicroMasters and a Microsoft specialization) evidences what I can actually build. Since a work sample predicts performance about 3× better than education, this live page translates those honors into an irrefutable legacy.
act1_s3_x: Three in four hiring teams say they receive AI-written applications, and 65% of hiring managers find skills harder to verify. When anyone can write a fluent claim in seconds, only a verifiable build stands out.
act1_foot: Sources: Sackett et al. (2022) on selection validity; Robert Half, November 2025, n = 2,000+; Deel Global Hiring Report 2026.
act2_verdict: Three levels of fidelity, one direction.
act2_lede: From renting a template to directing every line.
act2_s1_x: My first portfolios ran on Canva, Figma and Framer from 2023 to 2025. None matched the fidelity my design and my authority as a UX educator demanded, and learning to code meant a new degree and starting over as a junior.
act2_s2_x: It was never about prompting AI for a website to brag about. Weeks on this compact one-scroll page gave me the flight hours no university could, testing and locking the AI workflows that built the multi-page site you are reading.
act2_s3_x: The version you are reading: dedicated About and Contact pages, four copy-tested case briefs, my most capable front-end to date, and the Microsoft specialization finished.
act2_foot: Building a site with AI in 2027 takes more than a prompt: it takes a whole orchestration, from research to review. That is what sets this build apart from audacious vibe-coders and from developers who still write every line by hand.

sch_fn_commits: Commits. Un commit es un cambio guardado en el código del sitio, con una nota de lo que cambió. La cifra junto a cada etapa excluye los commits de integración. Cada barra va del primer commit de la etapa al último, y sus días activos son las fechas con al menos un commit.
sch_fn_prs: Pull requests. Un pull request es un conjunto de commits que se proponen juntos, se revisan y luego se integran al sitio en vivo. Los pull requests #18–#32 se agrupan en cinco etapas según lo que cambiaron. Cada rombo está en su fecha de integración en hora de Lima (UTC−5), por eso #24 y #29 caen un día antes que sus fechas UTC en GitHub.

act4_verdict: Four choices keep this site fast, open and easy to grow.
act4_lede: The decisions under every page, in plain words.
act4_c1_t: 1) No framework to weigh it down
act4_c1_x: The site runs on the web's own three languages, with no framework or add-on in between, so pages load fast and nothing breaks when a tool changes.
act4_c1_rv_txt: Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, served as static files: no build step, no framework and no dependency that cannot be read end to end. Nothing to migrate when a major version lands, no security-patch treadmill, and a light payload that stays fast on an average phone connection.
act4_c2_x: Anyone can move through every page with a keyboard or a screen reader, and text stays readable in light and dark themes, on a phone or a wide screen.
act4_c2_rv_txt: Built to WCAG AA: every meaningful image carries alt text, every control is reachable by keyboard with a visible focus state, and contrast is verified in both themes rather than assumed. Layout resolves at three declared breakpoints — 767px and below, 768 to 1023, and 1024 up.
act4_c3_x: Every word lives in one of three places: text every page shares, text every case brief shares, and text for one page only. Change a shared label once and it updates everywhere, in both languages.
act4_c3_rv_txt: Three dictionary levels merge in order: global site chrome, a regional layer for what the briefs share (interface labels, tags, related reading), then each brief's own local keys. A key lives at exactly one level, and every English file has a Spanish twin with the same keys, checked by script before each commit.
act4_c4_t: 4) The same templates on every brief
act4_c4_x: Every case brief uses the same interface components as templates: acts, cards, panels, charts and dashboards. A reader who learns one brief can read them all.
act4_c4_rv_txt: Each brief is its own page with its own route and dictionary, built from one shared set of components and design tokens. The trade-off is discipline: a defect in a shared component shows up in every brief, so each change is checked across all of them at three widths, two themes and two languages.

dash_r1: 286 commits pasaron por 52 gates de revisión. Nada se desplegó sin pasar antes un control que yo mismo me fijé.
dash2_r1: El build multipágina mantuvo ese hábito y partió de una lista escrita de defectos conocidos, no de cero.
dash_r3: Lo que gana un equipo no es este código. Es la forma de trabajar que hizo más barato el segundo build.

act6_lede: Tres lecciones sobre etapas, resoluciones y registros.
act6_p1_x: Cada ejecución se detiene en cada etapa hasta que la libero con una frase fija. La revisión ocurre sobre la página en funcionamiento, en ambos idiomas, antes de cualquier integración.
act6_p2_x: Every decision becomes a numbered ruling in one log, and every edit I make on disk is recorded. The project manager's role is absorbed.
act6_p3_x: The build only proved itself once every claim could be traced to its source and every sentence read by someone outside tech. Plain words turned the work into proof.
